inline_comments.comment: Commented-out debug log left in: `// logger.info(\`Story ${entry.id} absolute path: ${absolutePath}\`);`. Project rules require all debugging artifacts (commented-out code, active console/logger calls added for debugging) to be removed before merging. Delete this line.

`changedFile.replace(\`${repoRoot}/\`, '')` uses a hardcoded `/` separator to strip the repo-root prefix. On Windows, `node:path`'s `resolve()` produces backslash-separated paths (e.g., `C:\Users\user\project`), so the template literal `${repoRoot}/` never matches and `changedFile` is stored verbatim instead of as a relative path. Replace with `path.relative(repoRoot, changedFile)` (using the platform-aware `node:path`) to correctly handle both Unix and Windows paths.

`gitDiffProvider.getChangedFiles()` and `gitDiffProvider.getRepoRoot()` are launched concurrently via `Promise.all`, but `getChangedFiles()` already calls `getRepoRoot()` internally. Before `this.repoRoot` is cached, both parallel executions can race and each spawn a separate `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` subprocess. The standalone `gitDiffProvider.getRepoRoot()` call is redundant; `repoRoot` is already guaranteed to be cached by the time `getChangedFiles()` resolves. Drop the explicit `getRepoRoot()` from `Promise.all` and instead call `gitDiffProvider.getRepoRoot()` sequentially after `getChangedFiles()` resolves (the cache hit makes it synchronous in practice).

`ChangeDetectionService` is exported without any API-stability prefix, while `getChangeDetectionReadiness` in the adjacent block is re-exported as `experimental_getChangeDetectionReadiness`. Since `ChangeDetectionService` is an internal implementation detail wired up by the dev server (not intended for end-user consumption), it should use the `internal_` prefix — i.e., `export { ChangeDetectionService as internal_ChangeDetectionService }` — to be consistent with other internal exports in this file (`internal_fullStatusStore`, `internal_universalStatusStore`, etc.).

`vi.clearAllMocks()` is called in both `beforeEach` and `afterEach`, which is redundant. Per project convention, a single `beforeEach(() => { vi.clearAllMocks(); })` is sufficient to reset mock state before each test. The `afterEach` duplicate should be removed.

The empty `} catch {}` block silently swallows any error thrown while collecting story stats for the cancellation telemetry payload. Project rules require at minimum a `logger.debug(err)` call inside catch blocks so failures remain visible during troubleshooting, even for non-critical paths. Either log at debug level or add a short inline comment (e.g., `// best-effort; process is exiting immediately`) so the intentional swallow is explicit to future readers.

general_comments.comment: The `readiness.ts` module holds the change-detection readiness state as module-level singletons (`readinessDeferred`, `readinessState`). `ChangeDetectionService`'s constructor unconditionally calls `resetChangeDetectionReadiness()`, which creates a new deferred and discards the previous one. Any caller still awaiting the old `getChangeDetectionReadiness()` promise will be silently abandoned — that promise will never settle. This design implicitly requires exactly one active `ChangeDetectionService` instance at a time. Adding a JSDoc block on `resetChangeDetectionReadiness` (and ideally on `getChangeDetectionReadiness`) documenting this contract would prevent accidental misuse if a second service is ever instantiated (e.g., in tests that forget `internal_resetChangeDetectionReadiness` in `beforeEach`).
